source_snapshot.procedure: Check CRC/error counters, run ib_write_bw for five minutes, check counters again, and repeat on other ports.
source_snapshot.criteria: Bandwidth matches the specification during stress; the system remains workable with no system-event error after stress.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Use `ib_write_bw -a -d mlx5_0 --report_gbits -q 8 -s 1048576 -t 300` with truncated output, a peer server, and an insecure sshpass/disabled-host-key wrapper.

original_test_intent.purpose: Measure InfiniBand RDMA write bandwidth for five minutes on every approved ConnectX port and verify throughput, link/error-counter health, host/peer stability, and absence of unexpected platform events.
original_test_intent.target: Each explicitly mapped InfiniBand HCA port, its approved peer port/path and fabric, plus SUT and peer host health; not an Ethernet or RoCE path unless the owner changes the testcase scope.
original_test_intent.scope: One source-required five-minute write-bandwidth test per approved port with authoritative pre/post IB counter deltas and a comparable port/path reference.
original_test_intent.operation: Start a matching perftest server on the designated peer, run the client for the approved 300-second duration on one mapped port at a time, collect complete endpoints/counters/output/logs, then repeat independently for all ports.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: 300 seconds per approved port. Message-size sweep versus one fixed size, QP count, directionality, complete port count, and repetition order require owner confirmation.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every port meets its approved comparable bandwidth threshold without new IB symbol/link/receive/transmit errors, unexpected kernel/BMC events, peer/SUT instability, or residual test processes.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/peer and HCA/port/GID/LID/link/MTU mapping, firmware/driver/perftest versions, symmetric server/client commands, 300-second proof, complete throughput output, authoritative per-port counter deltas, CPU/NUMA placement, SUT/peer logs, and per-port comparison.
ambiguities: The source does not define peer address, HCA/port IDs, all-size versus fixed-size profile, QPs, directionality, CPU/NUMA binding, expected bandwidth, or all port count/order.
`ethtool -S ethX` may observe an associated Ethernet/IPoIB netdev rather than the tested InfiniBand physical port.
The linked repository path is an iPerf script, not evidence that it implements the required ib_write_bw workflow.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires peer/tool/version/path/counter mapping, full untruncated output, dedicated-fabric approval, five minutes per port, secure access, and authoritative IB counters. However, it repeats DeepSeek's `-t 300` profile while describing it as a 300-second run; upstream perftest defines `-t` as TX depth and `-D` as duration.

applicable_history.decision: Network stress requires explicit target/peer/path, parameters, isolation, duration, evidence, approval, and recovery; tool syntax must be version-validated.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The test is automatable after fabric setup, but the V2/DeepSeek option string cannot satisfy five minutes because `-t 300` sets TX depth. V3 requires symmetric server/client commands using the installed version's duration option—upstream `-D 300`—and one separately evidenced run for each mapped IB port.

available_now: The ConnectX/InfiniBand write-bandwidth purpose, five-minute duration, per-port repetition, error-counter comparison, and host-health criterion are explicit.
Read-only HCA/port/firmware/driver/link/GID/LID/MTU/NUMA inventory and baseline IB/kernel/BMC counters can be collected before traffic approval.
missing_inputs: SUT/peer HCA and physical-port mapping, peer address, fabric route/partition, link rate/width/MTU, GID index and InfiniBand-versus-RoCE confirmation
Installed matching perftest/rdma-core/driver/firmware versions and version-validated symmetric server/client syntax
Approved message-size mode, QP/queue depth, unidirectional/bidirectional scope, CPU/NUMA binding, 300-second behavior, port order/repetitions, and bandwidth threshold/tolerance
Authoritative IB counter set, dedicated/shared fabric isolation approval, peer owner/window, abort limits, and recovery
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The IB/fabric and performance owners supply mapping, profile, counters, and reference; SUT/peer service owners approve isolation, maintenance, limits, and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect `ibv_devinfo`, `ibstat`, sysfs RDMA netdev associations, port state/rate/MTU/GID/LID, firmware/driver/perftest versions, PCIe/NUMA locality, and authoritative counter baselines
Verify peer reachability and compare local/peer `ib_write_bw --help` output without starting bandwidth traffic
prohibited_until_closed: Do not interpret `-t 300` as five minutes, start traffic without a matching peer, guess mlx5_0/port/GID/netdev, truncate output, clear counters/logs, expose passwords, or disable SSH host-key verification
Do not use Ethernet counters as sole IB evidence, run on an unapproved shared production fabric, merge multiple ports into one result, or declare PASS without the port-specific reference
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Owners approve one symmetric per-port server/client matrix showing `-D 300` or the installed release's verified duration syntax, mapped endpoints, expected rate, counter sources and limits; a short connectivity-only dry run is labeled non-completion.

revision_candidate.test_name: Per-Port InfiniBand RDMA Write Bandwidth Validation
revision_candidate.purpose: Run a 300-second ib_write_bw workload on each approved ConnectX InfiniBand port and verify bandwidth, authoritative port-counter deltas, and SUT/peer health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Two compatible RDMA hosts on the approved InfiniBand path with mapped ConnectX ports, matching firmware/driver/perftest capability, healthy link/fabric, isolated capacity, and monitoring/recovery access.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every owner-listed physical IB port and its exact peer/path, tested and recorded separately. Ethernet/RoCE netdevs or other HCAs are outside scope unless explicitly mapped to the test.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Endpoint/port/GID/LID/MTU mapping, peer address and partition/route, tool versions, symmetric commands, message-size/QP/TX-depth/direction/binding profile, `-D 300` duration confirmation, counter set, per-port reference/tolerance, isolation/window approval, limits, and recovery owners.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: For one mapped port, capture authoritative baselines; start the matching peer server; run the client with identical applicable options, explicit peer and `-D 300` (or version-verified equivalent); capture complete client/server output and telemetry; stop cleanly; collect counter/log deltas; then repeat the full sequence for the next port. Keep `-t` only for an explicitly approved TX depth.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Verified IB endpoints and physical ports, active link at expected rate/width/MTU, compatible perftest, idle/dedicated path or approved isolation, synchronized clocks, healthy baseline, peer owner approval, exact rate criterion, and tested stop/OOB path.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Per-port identity/path and topology, versions, exact symmetric commands, start/end timestamps proving 300 seconds, full unfiltered throughput/CPU output, message/QP/TX-depth/binding settings, authoritative before/after IB counter deltas, SUT/peer kernel/BMC logs, process cleanup, and comparison result.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The owner-approved per-port/path bandwidth target for the same link rate/width/MTU, direction, message size, QPs, CPU/NUMA placement and tool version, plus approved zero/tolerance rules for each counter.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No insecure credential/SSH shortcuts, log/counter clearing, guessed path, production-fabric saturation, mismatched peer options, or continuation after error storms, wrong-port traffic, peer impact, thermal/CPU limit, link flap, or host instability.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Approval is required for SUT/peer selection, fabric isolation, server/client profile, per-port traffic window, expected bandwidth/counter rules, abort thresholds, and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners configure/authorize peer and fabric; after the matrix is fixed, endpoint checks, server/client orchestration, five-minute runs, counters, parsing and comparison are automatable.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Terminate both perftest processes, preserve partial outputs and counter deltas, remove only approved temporary binding/firewall settings, verify link/fabric and both hosts recover, and escalate unexpected errors before another port or retry.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Endpoint/path mismatch, incompatible options, unavailable peer, unapproved shared traffic, link below expected state, new IB error storm/link flap, wrong-port traffic, bandwidth/process anomaly, peer/SUT instability, thermal/CPU limit, missing duration proof, incomplete output, or unresolved counter mapping.

identified_defects: DeepSeek and V2 retain `-t 300` as if it were a five-minute duration; upstream perftest defines it as TX depth.
DeepSeek omits the client peer argument, truncates output, embeds a password, and disables host-key verification.
The source's ethtool counter may not represent the tested IB port.
The source does not define whether five minutes applies once per port and per message size, while the linked script points to iPerf rather than ib_write_bw.
reason_for_change: Correct a concrete CLI option error that would fail to execute the requested duration and define a symmetric per-port contract without guessing fabric or counter mappings.

new_technical_evidence.title: linux-rdma perftest manual
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Upstream ib_write_bw; installed release must be checked
new_technical_evidence.supports: `-D/--duration` runs for a specified number of seconds; `-t/--tx-depth` sets transmit queue depth; server and client mode-specific options must match and the client includes the server address.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The installed perftest version, supported options, peer address, port/GID mapping, and approved performance profile are unknown.

removed_ambiguities: Requires a complete independent 300-second evidence set for each port.
Distinguishes authoritative IB port counters from an arbitrary Ethernet netdev counter.
resolved_blockers: Missing peer/tools/mapping/reference remain provisionable readiness items, not permanent inability to automate the benchmark.
remaining_blockers: Traffic cannot start until the exact endpoints, versioned syntax, per-port profile/reference, counter mapping, fabric isolation, limits, and approval are complete.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 corrects V2's actionable duration-option error with upstream documentation, makes duration proof and per-port iteration explicit, and prevents Ethernet-counter or truncated-output false completion while retaining V2's classification, isolation, peer, security, and recovery gates.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source requires ib_write_bw for five minutes and repeats the complete check on other ConnectX ports.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 preserves the wrong `-t 300` example while intending 300 seconds; V3 requires the correct version-validated duration option and symmetric peer commands.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Isolate the fabric, map each port/peer, preserve full outputs and IB counter deltas, use secure access, and stop both endpoints on faults.
